final.memo:
We have reviewed the situation at the Company and have elected to pass. While the company operates as a local-commerce network, it currently functions as a melting ice cube with negative operating margins of -5.7% as of Q2 2016 [D01, D03]. In comparison to peers like eBay or TripAdvisor, the business suffers from a clear lack of profitable merchant retention and marketing efficiency [D05, D06].

Our valuation analysis highlights the disconnect between the current market capitalization of $2.97bn and the underlying economics [D04]. Based on 2016 EBITDA guidance, and applying a representative 8x multiple, the implied equity value remains in the $1.65bn-$1.85bn range, even after accounting for the $530.1m net cash position [D03, D04]. Without a clear catalyst, we see no path to bridging this valuation gap.

The investment case relies on an unspecified management team executing a multi-year turnaround without a defined governance route or board-level accountability [D01, D07]. Third Point requires a concrete event or an identifiable earnings inflection to justify engagement; here, we find neither [D01]. Consequently, we have no edge in this situation and choose to allocate our capital elsewhere.
